name: Adjacent Degree-Three Corner-Pair Descent
statement: Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes. If $c,u$ are adjacent degree-three corners, then each of $H\setminus\{c\}$, $H\setminus\{u\}$, and $H\setminus\{c,u\}$ is again an ample forbidden pc-minor. Consequently, a degree-three corner of a corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor has no corner as a neighbour.
proof: Adjacent corners share their unique maximal three-cube. Deleting both leaves an ample irredundant family $G$, and re-adding either tip has the same acquired two-coordinate support. Adjacent square-completion invariance makes $G$ nonpeelable. For every elementary pc-minor, the image of $H$ equals the image of $G$, or is obtained from it by one addition of support at most two, or by an adjacent pair whose common individual support has size at most two. Rank-two one-concept invariance and adjacent-pair invariance therefore make every proper elementary image of $G$ peelable, proving that $G$ is forbidden. Either single deletion is nonpeelable because a peeling could be prefixed by the deleted corner to peel $H$; the one-concept obstruction atlas then makes both single deletions forbidden. Adjacent corners have the same maximal cube and degree, so the terminality assertion follows.
